brief.headline: Sales since {period_start} are {yoy_ptd} vs last year; first-time Gen Z customers accounted for {genz_new_share} of the growth, and {top1_name} and {top2_name}, the two largest product gains, have under {risk_threshold} weeks of stock left.

items.text: Sales since {period_start} are {sales_ptd} against {sales_ptd_ly} on the same days last year ({yoy_ptd}); each week was ahead of the same week last year ({weeks_ahead} of {weeks_total}).

First-time Gen Z customers rose from {genz_new_customers_ly} to {genz_new_customers}. Sales from them are {genz_new_diff} vs last year, {genz_new_share} of total growth; {genz_new_store_share} of that change was in stores.
Returning Gen Z customers fell from {genz_repeat_customers_ly} to {genz_repeat_customers}, and sales from them are {genz_repeat_sales_yoy} vs last year ({genz_repeat_diff}).

{top1_name} ({top1_diff}) and {top2_name} ({top2_diff}) had the largest product gains; women's apparel is {apparel_yoy} vs last year, and {overstock_names} each have more than {overstock_threshold} weeks of stock.
This week so far is {wow} vs the same days last week and {wtd_yoy} vs the same days last year.
Week {last_week_no} was {last_week_yoy} vs last year, against {prior_week_yoy} the week before.
First-time Gen Z customers this week so far: {genz_new_wtd}, against {genz_new_last_week} on the same days last week.

Weeks of stock left fell from {top1_cover_prev} to {top1_cover} for {top1_name} and from {top2_cover_prev} to {top2_cover} for {top2_name}; families that changed stock status since last week: {status_changes}.

{top1_name} and {top2_name} accounted for {top12_growth_share} of total growth ({top12_diff} of {growth_ptd}); they have {top1_cover} and {top2_cover} weeks of stock left, against {top1_cover_ly} and {top2_cover_ly} last year, and {top1_name} sells {top1_rate} units a week with {top1_stock} in stock.
First-time Gen Z customers accounted for {genz_new_share} of growth, and {top1_name} and {top2_name} accounted for {genz_new_top12_share} of their gain ({genz_new_top12_diff} of {genz_new_diff}).

The share of first-time Gen Z customers in Insider fell from {genz_new_insider_ly} to {genz_new_insider}: online from {genz_new_insider_online_ly} to {genz_new_insider_online}, in stores from {genz_new_insider_store_ly} to {genz_new_insider_store}; for first-time customers of other generations, the share rose from {other_new_insider_store_ly} to {other_new_insider_store} in stores and from {other_new_insider_online_ly} to {other_new_insider_online} online.

Sales from returning Gen Z customers are {genz_repeat_diff} vs last year, {genz_repeat_store_diff} of it in stores, where their Insider share fell from {genz_repeat_insider_store_ly} to {genz_repeat_insider_store}; returning customers overall went from {repeat_customers_ly} to {repeat_customers}.

Greater China is {china_yoy} vs last year: first-time customers {china_new_diff}, returning customers {china_repeat_diff}. In Europe ({europe_yoy}) sales from both groups grew, {europe_new_diff} and {europe_repeat_diff}.
The online group of first-time Gen Z customers is small, {genz_new_online_customers_ly} last year and {genz_new_online_customers} this year, so its Insider share moves with a few customers.

Most customers appear once in this extract, so returning customers are identified by their customer status, not by a measured repeat rate; the data also does not say whether the Insider flag means member at purchase or today.

{scan1_name}: sales were {scan1_early_yoy} vs last year in weeks {scan_early_first}–{scan_early_last} and {scan1_recent_yoy} in weeks {scan_recent_first}–{scan_recent_last}; each of the last {scan1_streak} complete weeks was above the same week last year.

{scan2_name}: sales were {scan2_early_yoy} vs last year in weeks {scan_early_first}–{scan_early_last} and {scan2_recent_yoy} in weeks {scan_recent_first}–{scan_recent_last}; it has {top1_cover} weeks of stock left against {top1_cover_ly} last year.

{scan4_name}: sales were {scan4_early_yoy} vs last year in weeks {scan_early_first}–{scan_early_last} and {scan4_recent_yoy} in weeks {scan_recent_first}–{scan_recent_last}; each of the last {scan4_streak} complete weeks was above the same week last year.

{scan5_name} are {scan5_yoy} vs last year and {scan5_recent_yoy} in weeks {scan_recent_first}–{scan_recent_last}, below the same week last year in each of the last {scan5_streak} complete weeks; {scan8_name} are {scan8_yoy}, above last year in each of the last {scan8_streak} complete weeks.

{scan6_name} are {scan6_yoy} vs last year and {scan6_recent_yoy} in weeks {scan_recent_first}–{scan_recent_last}; {scan7_name} are {scan7_yoy}, and {scan7_recent_yoy} in the same weeks. The two groups have {scan6_customers} and {scan7_customers} customers.

The scan checks every region, product family, store vs online, full-price vs outlet and customer group, alone and in pairs; {scan_small_count} groups with a sizeable change were left out because they had fewer than {scan_min_customers} customers in either year.
